title: Audit activity chronicle: cursored search, filter presets, and CSV/NDJSON streaming export
creator: Marcus Chen
description: Background: The current audit viewer provides basic search and CSV downloads but struggles with high-volume exports (timeouts, memory spikes) and inconsistent RBAC scoping with RBAC v2. Goal: Implement a cursored search API with stable continuation tokens, add user-visible filter presets (saved queries), and provide a streaming export option that supports CSV and NDJSON to avoid server-side buffering. Scope: backend cursor API, export streaming endpoints, console UI for saved filters and export modal, RBAC enforcement on export and saved-queries, telemetry and cost guardrails. Out of scope: full-text reindexing and archive cold-storage exports (future work).
acceptance_criteria: Cursored search endpoint that returns stable continuation tokens and can page reliably across >10M events
Export endpoint streams results as CSV and NDJSON without loading entire result sets into memory
Console UX to save, edit, and apply filter presets tied to user/org and respect RBAC v2 scoping
Exports enforce permission checks (audit.read for org-level, audit.export for exports) and log export events
Pagination and export behavior documented in Console help and API reference
Load tests demonstrate export can stream 100k events/hour on current infra with <2% CPU tail variance
comments: 2026-02-25 Marcus Chen: Created ticket after postmortem from INC-2026-02-18 (export-timeout). Problem statement: ad-hoc CSV downloads caused worker OOMs and blocked UI. Proposed a streaming approach + cursored search to make exports resumable.

2026-03-02 Aisha Patel: Design sync with UX and Security. Decision: saved queries should be namespaced by org and optionally shared. RBAC v2 will introduce two export-level permissions (audit.read and audit.export). Security requested audit trail for export actions.

2026-03-04 Elena Rivera (Security): Reviewed RBAC mapping. Blocking item: need to update policy evaluation to short-circuit export endpoints to avoid leaking row-level data. Added ENG-49801 as dependency to land policy fixes.

2026-03-06 Dev note (Aisha): Prototyped streaming NDJSON export using chunked transfer. Initial tests show reduced memory usage but serialization CPU is a hotspot. Filed micro-optim PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6472

2026-03-09 QA (Jordan Kim): Ran basic end-to-end export test. NDJSON stream finishes for 50k rows in ~35s locally. Found edge case: saved query with many join filters returns incorrect continuation token — tracked under ENG-49970.

2026-03-12 Ops (Priya Singh): Load test on staging using exports-dashboard: sustained 10 concurrent exports of 100k events produced 18% network egress increase and CPU p95 up 12% on exporter workers. Recommend soft rate limiting per-org and an export-cost alerting rule.

2026-03-14 Aisha Patel: Moved ticket to In Progress. Implemented server-side cursor API (draft) and wired export modal in console prototypes. Next: polish RBAC checks, add telemetry, and prepare PR for review.
Links: design doc (Confluence), UX mocks (Drive), staging dashboard (Grafana), open PR (GitHub).
notes: Trade-offs: streaming avoids memory issues but adds operational complexity (partial downloads, retry semantics). We will emit export metadata so clients can resume by token.
Rollout plan: feature-flag backend + UI; enable export streaming for beta orgs; monitor export-related CPU/network metrics for 2 weeks before full release.
Fallback behavior: if streaming fails, UI will fall back to a capped preview export (max 5k rows) and surface error with instruction to contact support for bulk extracts.
